claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities", series "Defense Futures", published 2010-11-20 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2010-08-30, DIA document number DIA-08-1012-001. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Released PDF is 46 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).

The DIA list transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018 reads 'Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities, Dr W Culbreth, Univ of Nevada-Las Vegas.'

The released cover page carries the date 20 November 2010, an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 30 August 2010 and document number DIA-08-1012-001, in the 'Defense Futures' series; the author field is redacted under (b)(6).
George Knapp obtained and released this DIRD in mid-2019, making it the fifth AAWSAP deliverable in the public domain, nearly three years before DIA's bulk FOIA release of 25 March 2022.

It is the sensor-side counterpart to the cloaking and signature-reduction strand of the survey: Puthoff described the DIA Broad Area Announcement as specifying twelve threat areas including 'lift, propulsion, signature reduction, human effects and so on.'

connections.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
connections.note: The released document names the programme itself. Its inside cover reads 'This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' - the redaction between them is (b)(3):10 USC 424. Verified by downloading this DIRD and scanning its full text on 23 August 2026. The scans are OCR-degraded, so the quotation is normalised from the damaged rendering.

connections.label: Signals & Sensor Intelligence
connections.note: The sensor-side counterpart to Leonhardt's cloaking DIRD: one asks how an object could be made undetectable, the other how an object moving at hypersonic velocity could nevertheless be tracked at high resolution. Together they bracket the observability problem that any UAP sensor programme has to solve.
